name: Dandruff maxxing

card.summary: A scalp-care routine, mainly medicated shampoo and gentler hair products, aimed at clearing flaking so hair and shoulders look clean.
card.note: Persistent flaking, redness or hair shedding is a reason to see a dermatologist.

quick.overview:
Dandruff maxxing is the looksmaxxing term for treating scalp flaking so that hair looks cleaner and visible white flakes disappear from hair and dark clothing.

Dandruff is common, affecting roughly half of adults according to Wikipedia, and is linked to skin oil and the Malassezia yeast on the scalp. Routines center on shampoo choice and washing habits.
quick.how: Forum guides recommend a plain shampoo and conditioner rather than a 2-in-1 product, and mention anti-dandruff active ingredients such as zinc pyrithione. Dermatology references list ketoconazole, selenium disulfide, piroctone olamine, coal tar and salicylic acid as other shampoo actives. Results with any regimen usually come over weeks.
quick.risks: Shampoos can irritate some scalps, and one guide notes that stopping shampoo altogether may help some people and worsen others. Flaking with redness, or hair shedding, can have other causes such as seborrhoeic dermatitis or psoriasis.

lead: Dandruff maxxing is the looksmaxxing name for a scalp and dandruff care routine whose aim is flake-free hair and a cleaner-looking head of hair. [1]

Dandruff is a common scalp condition that causes flaking and sometimes mild itch; Wikipedia reports that it affects about half of adults and usually begins at puberty. [2] Its cause is described as a mix of genetic and environmental factors, including scalp oil and the activity of Malassezia yeast, and it is not due to poor hygiene. [2]

A looksmax.org guide lists irritated oily skin, dry skin, Malassezia, product sensitivity and conditions such as psoriasis and eczema as causes, and discusses shampoo selection and the "no shampoo" movement. [1]

chain: Reduce flaking with suitable shampoo and washing
angle.text: Visible white flakes on hair and dark clothing are removed or reduced, which makes hair look cleaner. Treatment is aimed at the scalp rather than the hair shaft.

infobox: Zinc pyrithione, ketoconazole, selenium disulfide, piroctone olamine

paras: The looksmax.org guide defines dandruff as flaking of scalp skin and recommends choosing a good shampoo and a separate conditioner rather than a combined product. The author names one brand as drying and another as his own choice. [1]

The guide also points out that zinc pyrithione is the active in many anti-dandruff shampoos. It describes the no-shampoo approach as a possible fix when shampoo itself is the irritant, though it may worsen flaking in others. [1]

sections.h: Causes and treatments in medical references
paras: Wikipedia states that skin cells in affected people may turn over in two to seven days rather than about a month, and that Malassezia globosa breaks down scalp oils into oleic acid that can trigger inflammation. [2]

Antifungal shampoo ingredients listed there include piroctone olamine, ketoconazole, zinc pyrithione and selenium disulfide, with coal tar and salicylic acid as exfoliating agents. Dry scalp is often mistaken for dandruff but has different causes. [2]
Replies to the guide ranged from jokes about the topic to mockery of the thread title, showing that dandruff is discussed with humor on the forum. [1]
No studies found specific to the looksmaxxing routine. Controlled trials of antifungal shampoos for dandruff exist in the dermatology literature and are summarized in general medical references. [2]

lore.intro: Looksmax.org members share shampoo recommendations and causes of flaking. [1]

claims.claim: Switching to a good separate shampoo and conditioner is usually the solution to dandruff.
claims.believers: The guide author says plain shampoo and conditioner solve most cases and that he uses one named brand. [1]
claims.experts: Wikipedia lists antifungal and exfoliating shampoo actives as the recognised treatments and describes dandruff as having genetic and environmental causes. [2]

claims.claim: Going without shampoo can resolve dandruff caused by shampoo.
claims.believers: The guide says the no-shampoo movement may help if the shampoo is the cause, but could make flaking worse. [1]
claims.experts: No published studies were identified on the no-shampoo method for dandruff.
